conclusion: **Classification: supported** for the narrow reported conclusion: these data do not support a positive vmPFC response under the specified whole-brain-corrected test. The protocol tests the positive group mean at the participant level (54 independent participants) across the common nonzero support using 5,000 sign flips and a one-sided maximum-t statistic. Support required a positive voxel inside a prespecified Harvard–Oxford vmPFC operationalization to pass whole-brain FWE p < .05. The report finds 0/6,174 vmPFC voxels passing; the descriptive ROI mean is −0.0103 (95% t interval −0.0290 to 0.0084; t(53)=−1.10; one-sided p=.862), with 21/54 positive participant averages. The strongest corrected positive voxel is outside the ROI (MNI [−26, −102, −3.6], mean 0.1121, t=6.62, max-t FWE p=.001). These findings support a lack-of-evidence conclusion at the prespecified threshold; they do not show that the true vmPFC effect is zero or rule out smaller effects.
